gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/final recommended=1

This PR adds an Export CSV button to the reports page that downloads a CSV built 100 rows at a time under a 4-second limit, and it answers "not found" for unknown reports. It covers the button and the paging and time limits, deliberately exports the 12 columns visible by default instead of all 40 because the full table is too wide, defers emailed exports and audit-log events to acme/widgets#46, and leaves the under-5-second speed on production data to be checked after merge.

Nothing blocks merging. The checks ran in CI on the commit being reviewed and passed, and the tests cover the exact 12-column header, escaped cells, the paging limit, the time limit and the unknown-report case. You are the author, so you cannot approve your own PR. One smaller point does not block merging: the export handler pages through rows with its own loop instead of reusing the shared paging helper, which duplicates logic the repository already has (src/api/export.ts, line 31). The fix nits row can take it.

I recommend merge because every requirement this PR owns is in place and the required check passed.

Pick one:
1. merge - squash-merge this PR at the commit being reviewed. [recommended]
2. fix nits - replace the duplicated paging loop with the shared paging helper in one repair pass, review it, push, and watch the checks.
3. stop - leave the PR open and the worktree as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves f1 from fails to holds: the opening is two plain sentences naming the Export CSV button, the 100-row/4-second paging bound, the deliberate 12-of-40 column choice, and the email and audit deferrals to acme/widgets#46, with no 'Delivers:' label and no 'ACs 1, 4' row numbers; Before failed on both the label and the numbered rows. Everything else (zero blockers, merge offered, no blocker on deferred/deviated rows, nothing posted) holds in both. One wording risk in After: the deviation reason is rendered as 'because the full table is too wide', which is not the spec's stated reason — the spec says the table has 40 columns and the 12 visible-by-default ones carry the fields most readers use. To keep the deviation reason grounded rather than invented, say 'deliberately exports the 12 columns visible by default instead of all 40, as the spec chose because those carry the fields most readers use'. Also, the fix-nits row now promises push-and-watch-checks, while Before promised one repair iteration then a return to this menu; keep the narrower 'one repair pass, then return to this menu' so the menu text matches the actual flow.
